tldr: Lighter news cycle today — 8 core items cleared the strict 48-hour filter (below the usual 10), and no standalone emerging-threat story met the novelty bar. Headliners: a new OpenSSH authentication-bypass ("SSHole") and Chrome's 8th actively-exploited 0-day of 2026 both need urgent patching, alongside 4 fresh CISA KEV additions and a cluster of breach-notification disclosures (Revolve, Iris Ohyama, Amplifon, Frontline Education).

items.title: OpenSSH "SSHole" auth-bypass under active exploitation
items.description: CVE-2026-123158 (CVSS 8.1) lets a 257–1024 char password bypass locked accounts, incl. root, on musl-libc/no-PAM systems (Alpine, OpenWrt, Buildroot, Yocto). Botnets already probing; added to CISA KEV Nov 9. Patch: OpenSSH 10.6p2.

items.title: Chrome patches 8th actively-exploited 0-day of 2026
items.description: CVE-2026-125350, a high-severity use-after-free in Chrome's XML component, is confirmed exploited in the wild. Fixed in Chrome 157.0.8103.50/.51 — update immediately. Not yet listed in CISA KEV.

items.title: QNAP confirms ongoing "Plex2Shell" NAS compromises
items.description: Attackers chain four Plex Media Server flaws (CVE-2026-96652/96654/96655/96656, in KEV since Oct 20) for unauthenticated RCE on QNAP NAS devices. QNAP says new victims are still being compromised this week. Fix: Plex 1.43.5+.

items.title: CISA adds 4 vulnerabilities to KEV catalog
items.description: OpenSSH CVE-2026-123158; IBM Aspera Faspex CVE-2026-123218 (CVSS 9.8, admin takeover); SignalWire FreeSwitch CVE-2026-116779; GPUStack CVE-2026-102895. Federal remediation due Nov 12, 2026. (Latter three single-sourced to CISA's own page.)

items.title: Revolve data breach notifications land — scope disputed
items.description: Online fashion retailer Revolve is notifying victims of a Sept 11, 2026 card-data breach (stolen card numbers/expiry dates). Company figures cite "at least 180,000"; a Texas AG filing tally suggests up to 1.5 million — unconfirmed as a national total.

items.title: Iris Ohyama cloud breach may affect up to 7.7M customers
items.description: Japanese retailer found an intrusion into a third-party cloud service on Oct 28; exposed names, addresses, phone, email, DOB and encrypted passwords (no card data). The 7.7M figure may be total stored records rather than confirmed victims; no misuse reported yet.

items.title: Amplifon Americas discloses breach exposing SSNs, health data
items.description: Filed with Vermont and Texas AGs this week; exposed data includes names, DOB, state IDs, health information, and for a limited subset, Social Security and financial data. National victim total (reported as 1.3M) is single-sourced and unconfirmed from state filings.

items.title: Frontline Education breach victim count escalates past 3 million
items.description: K-12 software vendor (10,000+ districts) breached via a third-party application flaw, exposing staff/student SSNs, addresses and emails. Original estimates of ~1.3M have been revised upward past 3 million as scope assessment continues.

action: Patch Chrome to 157.0.8103.50/.51 now (actively exploited 0-day). Update/patch OpenSSH to 10.6p2 — or disable password auth — on any musl-libc/no-PAM systems (Alpine, OpenWrt, Buildroot, Yocto); under active opportunistic exploitation. Update Plex Media Server to 1.43.5+ on QNAP/NAS deployments. Remediate the four new CISA KEV entries (OpenSSH, IBM Aspera Faspex, SignalWire FreeSwitch, GPUStack) by Nov 12, 2026 if applicable. Breach items (Revolve, Iris Ohyama, Amplifon, Frontline) warrant monitoring and credential-reset hygiene for affected users, but no urgent technical patching.
